guide.title: Guide: set up PayPal and test with the sandbox
guide.intro: The sandbox is PayPal's test environment: no real money moves, you pay with test accounts. Setup:

steps.account: Sign in at <link>developer.paypal.com</link> with the organiser's PayPal business account.
steps.app: Under Apps & Credentials, switch to Sandbox and choose Create App (type: Merchant). Copy the Client ID and the Secret into the fields Client ID and Client secret below.
steps.webhook: In the app, open Sandbox Webhooks → Add Webhook, enter the webhook URL shown below and select the events Checkout order approved and Payment capture completed / denied / refunded / reversed. Enter the displayed Webhook ID below. PayPal only reaches public HTTPS addresses – a local test system (localhost) receives no webhooks. Payments still work there, because they are completed when the buyer returns from PayPal; webhooks only cover buyers who close the PayPal window before returning.
steps.enable: Select the environment “Sandbox (test)”, switch on “Offer PayPal” and save. PayPal now appears as a payment method in the checkout.
steps.test: Test purchase: under Testing Tools → Sandbox Accounts PayPal creates a buyer account (“Personal”) automatically; e-mail and password are shown under “View/Edit account”. In the shop choose PayPal, click “Place binding order”, sign in on PayPal's test page with this buyer account and pay. You return to the order page and the order is paid. The money appears in the sandbox business account (sign in at sandbox.paypal.com).
steps.live: Going live: switch Apps & Credentials to Live, create an app with its own webhook there, enter the live client ID, secret and webhook ID and set the environment to “Live”. Sandbox and live credentials are different and cannot be mixed.

guide.title: Step-by-step setup guide
guide.intro: You need a paid Apple Developer Program membership. Allow about 20 minutes.

steps.account: Join the <link>Apple Developer Program</link> (paid, per year) with the Apple ID of your organisation.
steps.passType: Under Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Identifiers register a new Pass Type ID, for example pass.com.example.tickets, and enter it above.
steps.certificate: Create a signing request on your computer: openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout pass.key -out pass.csr -subj "/CN=Tickets". Open the Pass Type ID, click Create Certificate, upload pass.csr and download pass.cer.
steps.export: Convert the certificate to PEM: openssl x509 -inform DER -in pass.cer -out pass.pem. Paste pass.pem as certificate and pass.key as private key.
steps.wwdr: Download the Worldwide Developer Relations - G4 certificate from Apple (apple.com/certificateauthority) and convert it: openssl x509 -inform DER -in AppleWWDRCAG4.cer -out wwdr.pem. Paste it as WWDR certificate.
steps.upload: Enter your 10-character Team ID, switch Apple Wallet on and save.
steps.test: Click Check configuration, then place a test order and open the order page on an iPhone: the Add to Apple Wallet button installs the pass. Certificates expire after a year - the check warns 30 days before.

guide.title: Step-by-step setup guide
guide.intro: Free of charge; allow about 15 minutes. Images in Google passes are taken from the event image and the shop logo and only work when the shop is reachable via public https.

steps.console: Open the <link>Google Pay & Wallet Console</link>, sign in, create a business profile and accept the Google Wallet API terms.
steps.issuer: Copy the Issuer ID (Google Wallet API area of the console) into the field above.
steps.project: In the Google Cloud console create a project and enable the Google Wallet API there.
steps.serviceAccount: Create a service account in that project and add a JSON key to it. Download the key file.
steps.access: In the Wallet Console under Users invite the service account e-mail address with the role Developer.
steps.upload: Paste the JSON key above, enter the issuer ID, switch Google Wallet on and save.
steps.test: Click Check configuration. New issuers start in demo mode: passes are labelled test-only and can only be saved by test users added in the console. Request publishing access there before going live.

issues.issuerNoAccess: The service account has no access to issuer {issuerId}. Add it as a user in the Google Pay & Wallet Console.

design.title: Pass design (all events)
design.description: Colours, logo text and images of wallet passes. Individual events can override the design on their Wallet tab.
design.eventDescription: Overrides the global design for this event.
design.inheriting: This event currently uses the global design. Saving creates a dedicated design for this event.
design.logoTextHint: Shown next to the logo on Apple passes. Optional.
design.descriptionHint: Short description read by screen readers; defaults to the event title.
design.imagesHint: Apple Wallet only accepts PNG images; other formats are ignored. Without an icon a neutral square in the background colour is generated. Google passes use the event image and shop logo instead.

images.logoHint: PNG, e.g. 160 x 50 px (also used as icon when none is set).
images.iconHint: PNG, 58 x 58 px or larger (shown on the lock screen).
images.stripHint: PNG, e.g. 750 x 196 px banner behind the event title.
